### B. The 3 measures

`protection_msr_payouts_12m` (customer-wide payout sum over the rolling twelve months) is carried by
`the_rolling_twelve_month_payout_ceiling`. `protection_msr_claims_filed_term` (claims filed over the
coverage term, start to end inclusive) is carried by `when_a_claim_may_be_taken` cl. 6: "The claims filed
in a term are counted on the plan across its coverage term, from the coverage start day to the coverage end
day inclusive." `protection_msr_repair_attempts_item` (decisions settled by repair on the same serial over
the item's life) is carried by `bases_of_a_claim_decision`: "The repairs counted are the decisions recorded
as settled by repair on the same covered item serial, taken across the whole life of that item from its
purchase day to the day of handling."

carried as clauses in force. Nothing is retired that the source did not declare retired.

| `protection_premium_billing` (from `..._fleet_instalment_billing`) | "an instalment plan bills the monthly premium of the plan on the same day of each month" | `how_premium_is_billed_and_applied` cl. 2: "The clause of this rule providing that an instalment plan bills the monthly premium of the plan on the same day of each month is **no longer in force**, having been superseded by the current basis on which an instalment is priced. Correctly, no replacement text is restated inside a retired clause ("which is not restated here" in all

### D. The 4 extended policies this task's tree walks — baseline, then every factor

default constants rendered there and every product figure it reads named. Every factor's ladder is carried
whole in its own factor document, tier by tier, with each limb of each compound condition, each window and
each threshold in figures. Each factor document names no other document and no computation document hints
that anything modifies it.

**`protection_ext_premium_late_fee_scale` → `working_out_a_late_fee`.** Baseline carried verbatim in
substance: arrears as instalments billed less payments received to the cent never below nothing; unpaid
periods as whole periods with the part period not counted; fee per period = the plan's late fee; every
unpaid period counted; the plain rate of 100 percent; nothing written off; the assembly and the rounding.
Product figures named: "The monthly premium of the plan and the plan's late fee are the figures recorded
against that plan" — both rendered in `premium_tariff_schedule` (12.99) and
`premium_arrears_and_ending_fees` (12.00, and 30 grace days). Factors:

### F. The 6 prerequisites, each listed separately

Every `policy_source` sentence was matched **verbatim after whitespace normalisation** against the title
and content of all 385 published documents. Each occurs **exactly once**, in a document of the problem it
blocks, and in no document of any other policy. `condition`, `resolved_by`, `effect`, `kind` and `gate` are
authoring fields and appear nowhere in the corpus.

| # | Blocked problem | Waits on | Form | Carrying document (the blocked side's hub) | Occurrences in the whole corpus | Connective / strength |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `..._premium_arrears_settlement` | `..._premium_late_fee_scale` | `state` | `bringing_a_plan_premium_back_into_order` | 1 | "only after" — hard, matches |
| 2 | `..._claim_repair_settlement` | `..._premium_arrears_settlement` | `state` | `paying_an_approved_repair_claim` | 1 | "only once" — hard, matches |
| 3 | `..._spoilage_allowance` | `..._claim_repair_settlement` | `state` | `paying_the_food_spoilage_allowance` | 1 | "only after" — hard, matches |
| 4 | `..._claim_excess_settlement` | `..._claim_excess_charge` | `state` | `settling_the_excess_standing_against_a_claim` | 1 | "only after" — hard, matches |
| 5 | `..._fleet_invoice_settlement` | `..._fleet_instalment_billing` | `state` | `settling_a_premium_invoice_on_a_plan` | 1 | "only after" — hard, matches |
| 6 | `..._fleet_invoice_settlement` | `..._claim_excess_settlement` | `state` | `settling_a_premium_invoice_on_a_plan` | 1 | "only once" — hard, matches |

**Resolution basis for the three edges of task 0's tree** (each a `state` edge, so the depended-on
documents must describe, in the words the sentence uses for the state, the write that brings it about):

- Edge 3. Sentence: "The allowance for spoiled food is worked out only after every cost the claim has
  already been approved for stands booked as paid against the plan's cover." Words of the state: *a cost
  the claim stands approved for*, *booked as paid against the plan's cover*. Depended-on rule, in
  `paying_an_approved_repair_claim`: "Where a claim stands approved for repair on a covered item … the plan
  pays the part of the repairer's bill that the cover carries … The money comes out of the cover still
  available on the plan", and the recording paragraph: the entry "takes the same amount off the cover still
  available on that plan". Records: `find_protection_events` shows a `protection_claim_decision` of
  `approved_repair` on `SC-2026-88413` and no `protection_claim_payout` against that reference. Resolvable,
  at the same strength, from the sentence + the depended-on rule + the records.
- Edge 2. Sentence: "The amount the plan pays on the claim is released only once no premium period covering
  the day the failure happened stands unpaid on the plan." Words: *a premium period covering the day the
  failure happened*, *stands unpaid on the plan*. Depended-on rule, in
  `bringing_a_plan_premium_back_into_order`: bringing the premium "back into order", the payment "applied
  from the oldest unpaid premium period given", "the premium still owed on the plan falls by the amount
  paid" — reinforced by base law in `how_premium_is_billed_and_applied` cl. 5 and
  `unpaid_instalments_and_grace` cl. 3. Records: the charge for `period_start 2026-08-08`/`period_end
  2026-09-07` with payments stopping at `period_start 2026-05-08`. Resolvable at the same strength.
- Edge 1. Sentence: "The amount the customer settles is fixed only after every fee owed for a period that
  has run past grace stands billed on the plan." Words: *a fee owed for a period that has run past grace*,
  *stands billed on the plan*. Depended-on rule, in `billing_a_late_fee_on_an_instalment_plan`: "A late fee
  falls due on a Northbeam ShieldCare Protection Plan whose premium instalments have run past grace … The
  entry raises the premium the customer still owes on that plan by the amount billed." Grace days from
  `premium_arrears_and_ending_fees`, counted per `unpaid_instalments_and_grace` cl. 1. Records: no fee entry
  on the plan (every `protection_premium_charge` carries `premium_kind: 'monthly_instalment'`). Resolvable
  at the same strength.

**The depended-on side never discloses who waits on it**: `billing_a_late_fee_on_an_instalment_plan`,
`bringing_a_plan_premium_back_into_order` and `paying_an_approved_repair_claim` each carry only their own
rule and, where they are themselves blocked, only their own prerequisite sentence. Confirmed by the
one-occurrence count above.

## kb_to_source

Every normative sentence of the 79 documents was traced to a structured source. Below are the results of
the sentence-by-sentence sweep, then the specific checks the skill requires on the prerequisite side.

### 1. Nothing added as procedure

Mechanical sweep of the whole protection corpus for `confirm`, `notif`, `verif`, `review again`,
`double-check`, `make sure`, `remind`, `advise the customer`, `explain to`, `escalat`, `should then`,
`must then`, `ask the customer`: every hit is either a tool-return description ("A single **confirmation**
sentence in plain text", in all eight hubs, which each tool's docstring also states) or source text
(`cancelling_a_plan_and_what_comes_back`'s free-look "confirmed within the plan's free look days", from
`protection_cancellation_refund`; `escalation_of_a_repeated_late_fee`'s "Rates of escalation", from the
source's own `escalation_pct`). **No** added confirmation, review, notification, re-check, escalation or
follow-up step anywhere. Sweep for route phrasing (`first call`, `call … tool`, `unless otherwise`,
`adjustments may apply`, `set out elsewhere`, `certain customers`, `may qualify`, `see the document`,
`step 1`, `before you`, `you should then`, `next,`): **no hits at all**.

### 2. One addition that changes the domain — recorded as RED

`the_allowance_a_managed_care_agreement_carries`, table row 2 (line 9 of its content):

> `| such an agreement, one carrying at least 1 included visit in its term, and no visit stands drawn on it inside that time | 30.00 |`

The source's ladder tier and the source's own rule sentence both read, without the inserted clause:

> `factors[managed_care_allowance].ladder[1].when`: "the profile holds such an agreement and no visit
> stands drawn on it inside that time"
> `rule`: "it is thirty dollars where the profile holds such an agreement and no visit stands drawn on it
> inside that time"

The KB has inserted ", one carrying at least 1 included visit in its term,". The nearest antecedent of the
source's "such an agreement" is tier 1's "a care agreement whose included visits run to 12 or more in its
term", so on the source's prose alone tier 2 reaches only a 12-or-more agreement; on the KB's prose it
reaches any care agreement carrying at least one included visit. The KB then asserts the widened reading
twice more:

> "one carrying 11 included visits is not, and with no visit drawn inside that time it reaches the middle
> row at 30.00" (lines 15–16)
> `| 6 | no | 30.00 |` (line 26 of the combinations table)

Neither an 11-visit nor a 6-visit agreement reaching 30.00 is stated anywhere in the source's rule or
ladder. The threshold figure `1` exists in the source **only** in the executable binding
(`care_allowance: … (care_visits or 0) >= 1 and care_visits_drawn <= 0 …`), which the KB is matching.
This is therefore a place where the source's `ladder`/`rule` prose and the source's own binding say
different things, and the KB has resolved it silently in favour of the binding, stating a threshold in
figures that the normative prose never states.

**Judgement.** At the level of entailment against the source's executable basis the KB is *correct*, and
across the domain it is the source's prose that is loose. But it is a normative claim the KB states in
figures where its normative source states none, and it widens a tier's reach on the reading a careful
reader of the source's prose would take. Recorded as **`KB-BIJECTION RED` (1 finding)**, with the
policy-side origin noted honestly in `bijection_verdict` and Step 4 below. It does not affect either task's
scored number: task 1's profile holds a 12-visit agreement with visits drawn, so tier 1 governs; task 0
computes no excess at all.

### 3. Three added definitional sentences — traced, and faithful

Each states a definition the source supplies elsewhere for the same notion, and none changes any permitted
action, parameter, order or result anywhere in the domain.

| Added sentence | Document | Structured source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "A claim deductible stands unsettled where the excesses billed on the plan come to more than the excess payments received against them." | `the_household_excess_on_spoiled_food` | The source's spoilage ladder says only "no claim deductible stands unsettled on the plan". The netted formulation is the source's own, for the same notion, in `protection_ext_claim_excess_settlement`'s rule ("every excess standing unsettled on the plan, the excesses billed on it less the excess payments received") and in the spoilage policy's own bindings `deductible_billed: SUM(…'protection_deductible_charge')` / `deductible_paid: SUM(…'protection_deductible_payment')`. Same-source equivalent restatement |
| "The average of the instalments billed inside the last 3 months is the total of those instalments divided by the number of them, taken to the cent; where no instalment stands inside those 3 months the divisor is taken as 1." | `the_price_of_a_period_billed_in_advance` | Source binding `advance_price: … RND(instalments_3m_total / MX(1, instalments_3m_count), 2) …`. Exact |
| "The repairs authorised on the item are the claim decisions recorded on the plan as settled by repair." | `the_share_of_parts_the_plan_meets` | Source binding `repairs_authorised: COUNT('protection_events', event_type='protection_claim_decision', settlement_basis='repair')`. Exact, including the plan scope |

### 4. Counting conventions rendered from the bindings — faithful

### 5. Nothing dropped or rewritten

No clause of any base or extended policy is unborne; no ladder tier is missing, merged, rounded or
softened; no method tier is compressed into "calculated accordingly"; no threshold is named under a
business term without its figure; no compound condition is reduced to one limb. The one place where the
prose adds rather than drops is §2.

## Further problems found (outside the three verdict categories)

Reported because the remit is to find and report every problem, and marked with the layer each belongs to.

### P1 — Policy side: the charge aggregates the compute reads carry no job filter, so the rule and its executable basis disagree

The extended rule, and the KB faithfully after it, scope the repairer's entries to one job:

> `rule` / `working_out_a_repair_claim_payout`: "The covered bill is the labour, the parts and the
> attendance charges booked against the job on the covered item inside the window read"

The bindings read every such row on the profile, with no `service_agreement_id` filter:

```
labour_billed:     XSUM('service','service_events','charge_amount', within_months=bill_window_months, event_type='service_labour_charge')
parts_base:        XSUM('service','service_events','charge_amount', within_months=bill_window_months, event_type='service_parts_charge') if (parts_entries >= 2 and …)
attendance_billed: XSUM('service','service_events','charge_amount', within_months=bill_window_months, event_type='service_fee_charge')
parts_entries:     XCOUNT('service','service_events', within_months=bill_window_months, event_type='service_parts_charge')
```

— against two sibling bindings in the same policy that **do** filter by job:

```
diagnoses_recorded: XCOUNT('service','service_events', within_months=12, event_type='service_diagnostic_record', service_agreement_id=covered_item_job)
visits_drawn:       XCOUNT('service','service_events', within_months=12, event_type='service_visit_consume',    service_agreement_id=covered_item_job)
```

Task 0's profile carries two TechWorks jobs — `217bbe00…` on the covered refrigerator serial and
`f453ddd1…` on an unrelated television (`NBTV5510-8830216`, labour 210.00 and parts 155.00 on 2026-01-14) —
so the two readings come apart, and the source layer's own record says so. The `factor_trace` for
`repairer_bill_window` reads:

> "The baseline reads the last twelve months, **which would pull in the January labour of 210.00 and parts
> of 155.00 from the television job** and give 1470.00 once the ceiling bit."

Two consequences for this audit:

- **The declared `baseline_result` of 721.95 is not the number the published baseline document yields.** On
  the rule's own job scope with the baseline 12-month window, the fall-back is labour 385.00 at 90 percent
  = 346.50 plus the most recent parts entry 248.60 at 75 percent = 186.45 plus no attendance = **532.95**.
  721.95 is 385.00 + 210.00 = 595.00 of labour at 90 percent (535.50) plus the same 186.45 — i.e. the
  customer-scoped figure. The fall-back a solver actually computes is still definite and still different
  from the scored 1248.90, so the blind audit is unaffected; but the baseline of record and the corpus
  disagree by 189.00.
- **On the corpus as published, the `repairer_bill_window` factor bears no weight on task 0's scored
  number.** Job-scoped, every entry on job `217bbe00…` (parts 2026-09-10 and 2026-09-12, labour 2026-09-10,
  trip charge 2026-09-10) falls inside 6 months *and* inside 12, so substituting the baseline window leaves
  the answer at 1248.90. The declared sensitivity of 1470.00 exists only under the customer-scoped
  aggregate. That is a weight-bearing question for the source layer, not a translation failure: the KB
  carries the factor's whole ladder, and it is findable from the records.

The faithful side is the rule, and the KB is on it. No KB verdict changes.

### P2 — Policy side: `attendance_billed` takes every service fee row, not the attendance charges the rule names

The same binding above sums **all** `service_fee_charge` rows. In the TechWorks event vocabulary that
event type also covers a no-show fee, a reschedule fee, a cancellation fee, a haul-away fee and a
diagnostic fee, none of which is an attendance charge. Task 0's job carries exactly one fee row — the
89.00 `trip_charge` — so the figure is right here; across the domain the compute is wider than both the
rule and the KB.

### P3 — Render side: "attendance charges" is never defined in this product's own words

`working_out_a_repair_claim_payout` and `the_share_of_attendance_charges_the_plan_meets` both turn on "the
attendance charges booked against the job", and neither they nor any other protection document says which
kinds of service charge those are. The only document in the whole 385-document KB that names a trip charge
as an attendance charge belongs to another product and expressly scopes the statement to its own
measurement: `docs/membership/circle_credit_attendance_charges_0fdff30b.json` — "A trip charge and an
after hours surcharge are the only two attendance charges read here, and each is taken as it stands on the
job." The TechWorks corpus calls its own charge "the crew attendance charge" and prices it at 59.00 for
`TechWorks Appliance Install and Haul Away`, while the booked row is a `trip_charge` of 89.00, so the
figures do not corroborate the identification either. On task 0 the mapping is forced by elimination (one
non-labour, non-parts row on the job, for bringing the crew out) and the scored number is safe; on a job
carrying a no-show fee and a reschedule fee beside a trip charge it would not be. Recorded as a
domain-level determinacy gap on the findability side.

### P4 — Render side: illustrations that sit very close to the seeded world

Not a breach of any check above — every illustration is labelled hypothetical and none reproduces a seeded
row — but worth recording as a leak risk.

- `the_ceiling_on_a_spoilage_allowance`: "A plan whose term limit is 6500.00 and whose food spoilage cover
  is 350.00 has 1400.00 of cover left and one allowance paid out as money to the customer four months ago"
  — task 0's plan carries a 6500.00 term limit, a 350.00 food spoilage cover, 1470.00 of cover left and one
  such allowance five months back, and sits on the tier the illustration selects.
- `the_price_of_a_period_billed_in_advance`: "A plan whose monthly premium is 39.00 has instalments of
  43.68, 41.34 and 45.00 billed inside the last 3 months" — 39.00 is task 1's plan's monthly premium,
  **41.34 is the instalment task 1 requires the solver to compute**, and 43.68 is that computation's
  declared per-factor baseline for `trading_record_window`. A solver reading this factor document is shown
  the scored figure of a sibling computation on the same task, beside that plan's own monthly premium.
- `the_discount_earned_by_the_trading_record`: the case row "18400.00 | active | 6 percent" against task
  1's actual merchandise total of 18420.00, on the same tier.

### P5 — Policy side: two extended policies both price a ShieldCare instalment period, at different figures

`protection_ext_fleet_instalment_billing`'s rule is general — "The instalment for a premium period on a
plan held on instalments …", with nothing confining it to the fleet tier, which the KB renders faithfully
as "a Northbeam ShieldCare Protection Plan held on instalments"
(`working_out_a_premium_instalment`, `billing_a_premium_instalment_period`). On task 0's plan that rule
would price a period at 12.99 raised by the 15 percent claims loading (payouts of 5030.00 in the year, 3
claims filed) and lowered by nothing, that is 14.94, while `protection_ext_premium_arrears_settlement`
prices the period taken ahead at 12.99 less the 5 percent membership discount, that is 12.34. The two
policies claim different subjects (`protection_premium_charge` against `protection_premium_payment`) and
the arrears baseline pins which figure its own settlement uses ("the periods taken ahead priced at the
plan's monthly premium less the discount allowed on them"), so nothing on task 0's world is ambiguous. But
the overlap is real in the domain, and it is on the policy side: the KB renders each rule in its own
document, exactly as written.

### P6 — Policy side: two prose-versus-binding ambiguities the KB resolved silently

Both are the class the render report itself flagged: a loose source sentence pinned to the executable
reading. One is harmless, one is finding B1.

- `household_excess_on_food`'s tier says only "no claim deductible stands unsettled on the plan". The KB
  supplies the netted definition. Harmless: the netted reading is the only available one, it is the
  source's own formulation for the same notion in the sibling policy, and the plan's `deductible_outstanding`
  field agrees with it on task 0 (0.00 against 225.00 − 225.00). Worth noting that where the plan's running
  field and the netted entries disagree — as `premium_outstanding` does on this very plan (38.97 against
  51.96) and as `visits_remaining` does on task 1's care agreement (9 against 12 − 2) — the gloss silently
  settles the question in the ledger's favour, and the source's prose alone would not.
- `managed_care_allowance`'s tier 2 says only "such an agreement". That one is **B1**.

### P7 — Policy side: soft boundaries the source leaves open and the KB correctly leaves open

`loading_window_counted`'s tier 1 says "the claims are counted **from the month** the cover was most
recently put back" — a month rather than a day, in the source's own words and the KB's. Immaterial on task
1 (the reinstatement is 2026-02-10 and both counted claims are filed in March and August 2026), but the
boundary is soft on both sides. Correctly, the KB does not close what the source leaves open.

### P8 — Policy side: a record inconsistency in task 1's seeded world

`service_agreements.701cb1ea…` carries `visits_remaining: 9`, while its own service ledger shows a
`service_visit_allowance_grant` of `visits_delta 12` and two `service_visit_consume` rows of −1, which nets
to 10. Recorded here because it bears on a factor of this product: a solver who reached for the agreement's
own field instead of the TechWorks entitlement schedule would fall out of the 12-or-more tier and, because
visits *are* drawn inside the year, out of the 30.00 tier too, reaching no allowance at all and an excess
of 262.50 instead of 202.50. The source binding uses the variant parameter
(`CPARAM('service','included_visits_per_term', status='scheduled')`), and the KB's "the included visits its
term carries" points at the term's entitlement rather than the remainder, so the corpus is on the right
side; the inconsistent record makes the distinction harder to trust than it needs to be.

### P9 — Base law stating an order, rendered as the source has it

`protection_premium_delinquency` contains, as base law, "A claim whose incident day falls inside an unpaid
period is not paid until that period is settled", and `unpaid_instalments_and_grace` cl. 3 renders it. Per
this skill the KB may neither drop nor soften base law, so this is a policy-side note and never a KB
verdict: the base clause independently asserts the same ordering that edge 2's prerequisite sentence
carries on the blocked side. The KB adds nothing to it and names no tool, no problem and no route beside it.

### P10 — A decisive reading the corpus leaves to inference

The ceiling tier that decides task 0's answer turns on "an allowance already stands paid out as money to
the customer on the plan inside the last 12 months". The source binding is
`prior_allowances_12m: SUM('protection_events','payout_amount', within_months=12,
event_type='protection_claim_payout', settlement_basis='reimbursement')`, so the notion is a
`reimbursement`-basis payout. The corpus never says so in terms; the reader must put together
`paying_an_approved_repair_claim`'s definition of `reimbursement` ("money paid to the customer instead of
goods or work") with `paying_the_food_spoilage_allowance`'s description of the allowance ("as money paid to
the customer for food spoiled by the failed appliance"). The inference is available and the alternative is
not equally supported, so this is not a red light — but the reading is worth 46.10 on task 0 (206.10 against
the 160.00 the other reading gives), which makes it the thinnest join in the corpus.

## Step 4 — settling the problems

- **Never accommodate in reverse.** B1 is reported as a defect of the document, not as a reason to change
  the policy. Where the document and the policy conflict, the policy is the faithful side.
- **Never dissolve a contradiction by hiding one side.** P1, P2, P5, P6 and P7 are contradictions or
  softnesses that originate on the policy side — a rule against its own bindings, a rule against a sibling
  rule, prose against an executable threshold. None is reported as something the documents should paper
  over, and no repair is proposed for any of them.
- **Report policy-side problems without letting them change this skill's verdict.** P1–P2 and P5–P9 are
  policy-side; they are recorded with their evidence and they leave this skill's verdict where the
  document-side evidence puts it.
- **Never recommend more than the source states.** Nothing above proposes naming a tool, a resolving
  problem or a route, and nothing proposes deleting a prerequisite sentence.
- **Nothing is attributed to a solving agent.** No finding rests on how a rollout behaved.

### 1. B1 — CLOSED, on both sides

**The source was amended in favour of the prose, which is the direction revision 1 reported as faithful.**
The ladder now reads:

```
managed_care_allowance.ladder:
  1: "the profile holds a care agreement whose included visits run to twelve or more in its term
      and a visit stands drawn on it inside the last twelve months"                   -> sixty dollars
  2: "the profile holds a care agreement whose included visits run to twelve or more in its term
      and no visit stands drawn on it inside that time"                               -> thirty dollars
  3: "otherwise, including a profile holding a care agreement whose term carries fewer than twelve
      included visits"                                                                -> no allowance
```

and the binding now tests the same threshold on both paying tiers, the figure `1` having gone:

```
care_allowance: "K('care_allowance_full_usd') if ((care_visits or 0) >= K('care_visits_threshold') and care_visits_drawn >= 1)
                 else (K('care_allowance_part_usd') if ((care_visits or 0) >= K('care_visits_threshold') and care_visits_drawn <= 0) else 0.0)"
```

The prose-versus-binding conflict that produced B1 no longer exists: `rule`, `ladder` and binding now say
the same thing.

**The KB matches the amended source exactly.** `the_allowance_a_managed_care_agreement_carries` now reads,
at content lines 8–10:

> `| every other profile, including one holding a care agreement whose term carries fewer than 12 included visits | no allowance for a managed care agreement is allowed |`
> `| a care agreement whose included visits run to 12 or more in its term, and no visit stands drawn on it inside the last 12 months | 30.00 |`
> `| a care agreement whose included visits run to 12 or more in its term, and a visit stands drawn on it inside the last 12 months | 60.00 |`

The three assertions revision 1 cited as the finding are each gone and each replaced by its correct
counterpart:

| Revision 1 | Revision 2 |
| --- | --- |
| `\| such an agreement, **one carrying at least 1 included visit in its term**, and no visit stands drawn … \| 30.00 \|` | `\| a care agreement whose included visits run to **12 or more** in its term, and no visit stands drawn … \| 30.00 \|` |
| "one carrying 11 included visits is not, and with no visit drawn inside that time it **reaches the middle row at 30.00**" | "one carrying 11 is not, and **falls to the last row, where no allowance is allowed**" |
| combinations row `\| 6 \| no \| 30.00 \|` | combinations rows `\| 4 \| no \| none \|`, `\| 4 \| yes \| none \|`, `\| 9 \| no \| none \|`, `\| 18 \| no \| 30.00 \|`, `\| 18 \| yes \| 60.00 \|` |

Corpus-wide, `at least 1 included visit` and `at least one included visit` occur in **zero** of the 385
published documents. The five combination rows are each correct on the amended ladder, and the table no
longer prints 12 as a worked case (only as the ladder threshold, where the render contract requires it).

The hard-coded variant name is gone from the charter — `care_agreement_job` is now
`CFIELD('service','service_agreement_id', status='scheduled')` — and the charter carries a new rule sentence
for the read, which the KB carries verbatim at lines 3–4: *"The care agreement read is the one standing
scheduled on the profile, and the included visits it carries are the visits its own term allows rather than
the visits left on it."* Revision 1's item-2 exposure is therefore closed at its root rather than merely
being immaterial: there is no variant name left to diverge from, and the tier-2 widening that would have
opened the gap is gone.

**On revision 1's own P1 write-up.** The source-layer auditor's disclosure is accepted and this auditor's

what the published baseline yielded, and stated that `repairer_bill_window` bore no weight on the published
reading. What it then did was grade the whole item "compute-side, scored answer unaffected" and file it as a
policy-side note. That grading was too mild for what the evidence already showed: a declared baseline that
the corpus does not yield, and a declared factor that the corpus leaves inert, are not bookkeeping
discrepancies — they are the two symptoms by which a mis-scoped aggregate hides from a weight test, since
substituting a baseline into a compute that carries the same mis-scoping on both sides of the substitution
cancels it out. Revision 1 should have said that the weight evidence for that factor could not be trusted at
all while the scoping disagreed, instead of reporting the inertness as a curiosity. The finding was right and
its consequence was understated.

### 3. The reordering discipline — PASS, and no reading loosened

Mechanically, across all 39 factor documents: exactly **two** have a ladder table whose rows no longer run in
the source's tier order, and both are the two documents the brief says were rewritten —
`the_allowance_a_managed_care_agreement_carries` and `the_share_of_attendance_charges_the_plan_meets`. Every
other ladder table is tier-1-first. Where a reordering is reported in the other 18 documents, it is the
**worked-case** table, not the ladder.

Whether a reordering can loosen a reading turns on whether the ladder's tiers are mutually exclusive as
written, or whether a later tier is only intelligible after an earlier one has failed. Sweeping all 39:

- **Two ladders are order-dependent**, because a later tier's condition is a superset of an earlier one's:
  `the_share_met_for_promptness_of_the_report` ("reported inside 3 days" / "reported inside 7 days" — a
  3-day report is also inside 7) and `the_share_of_labour_the_plan_meets` ("less than a third" / "less than
  two thirds" — an item under a third is also under two thirds). **Both retain their ladder tables in source
  tier order**, and both retain the sequential prose that makes the order explicit: *"a report made on the
  4th day is not, and falls to be tested against the 7 days"*, and *"An item of exactly 12 whole months has
  not run less than a third, so it falls to the second row"*. Only their worked-case tables were reordered,
  which cannot affect a reading.
- **The other 37 ladders are mutually exclusive on some limb** — theft above/no more than ten times, drawn/not
  drawn, statement closed/not closed, active/in grace, board-level/not board-level, above/at-or-above a
  fraction, and so on — so their row order carries no meaning and the two reversed tables cannot loosen
  anything. In both reversed tables the residual row also names its excluded case explicitly ("every other
  profile, **including one holding a care agreement whose term carries fewer than 12 included visits**";
  "every other plan"), so it does not have to be read as residual to be read correctly, and both documents
  retain a prose paragraph stating the logic in the original direction (*"a single drawn visit inside the
  last 12 months is enough to bring the share from the whole of the charges down to 60 percent"*).

**Does the discipline itself leak?** No, and the reason holds here as the sibling auditor found it
elsewhere. The ordering is stated without reference to any customer: no document names a customer, asserts a
tier assignment, or says which row is the usual one. A reader who does not already know the answer cannot
recover "this first row is not the governing one" from the fact that a table has an order — every table has
one. The claim was also tested numerically rather than taken on argument: no reordered table's rows produce
any scored value or intermediate of either task (§5).

Arithmetic was re-verified in every reordered table and every re-originated worked example across all 39
factor documents and all 8 baselines. **Every figure checks.** Spot record: 120 − 70 = 50 over a monthly
premium of 10.00 gives 5 whole periods and 7.50 × 5 × 100 percent = 37.50; a term limit of 8000.00 gives
2400.00 and 4000.00, and the five ceiling rows (5200/none → 260.00; 3900/none → 130.00; 3900/one → 260.00;
2100/one → 260.00; 180/one → 180.00) are each correct on the ladder; 450.00 × 40 percent × 80 percent −
30.00 = 114.00 with room 8000.00 − 2200.00 = 5800.00; a repair-attempts figure of 2 gives 5 → 75 percent,
3 → 75 percent, 2 → 90 percent, 1 → 90 percent, 0 → 100 percent on parts of 400.00; 16.12 + 15.74 + 17.03
averaged over three is 16.30; 149.00 × 1.5 = 223.50 on a theft settled at 1100.00 against ten times 149.00;
a failure on the 4th reported on the 9th, completed on the 27th and decided on the 30th gives 26, 18 and 23
days on the three rows.

### 4. P3 — the attendance-charge definition

The charter now carries the definition as a sentence of the repair-settlement rule, and
`working_out_a_repair_claim_payout` carries it verbatim as item 3 of its numbered definition:

> "The attendance charges are the trip charge, the after hours surcharge and the mileage beyond the covered
> radius booked on that job; a no-show fee, a reschedule fee, a cancellation fee, a haul-away fee and a
> diagnostic fee are not attendance charges and the plan meets none of them under this head."

Three kinds in, five out, matching the binding's three `charge_kind` filters exactly
(`trip_charge`, `after_hours_surcharge`, `out_of_radius_fee`). One closed derivation follows from it in the
worked example — *"Had a haul-away fee of 45.00 stood on the same job, it would not enter the covered bill
at all, because a haul-away fee is not an attendance charge"* — and **no trip-charge, crew-attendance or
mileage figure is restated**: the example uses an after hours surcharge of 80.00 and a haul-away of 45.00,
and neither the 59.00 on task 0's job nor the TechWorks rate card's own figures appear.

The renderer's claim that the product "now relies on no other product's document" is accurate **as to this
definition**, and should be read no wider. `after hours surcharge` now occurs in the protection corpus
itself, where at revision 1 the only document in the whole KB naming a trip charge as an attendance charge
belonged to another product and was scoped to its own measurement. The product still, and correctly, names
other products' records where a cross-difficulty factor's tier rests on them — the TechWorks entitlement
schedule for included visits, the Circle tier's protection plan discount, the Net Thirty terms and purchase
order requirement — which the render contract requires rather than forbids. The mapping from "the mileage
beyond the covered radius" to the record's `out_of_radius_fee` is available from the service corpus's
"covered radius" and "mile beyond" and from the field's own name.

The sharpened test: a leak applies the task's **governing tier** to the task's **actual base** and yields a
**scored value or intermediate** — all three together. Every figure in the corpus that coincides with a
value either task touches was triaged against it.

| Printed figure | Where | Governing tier? | Actual base? | Yields a scored value or intermediate? | Verdict |

| 125.00, 75.00 | `cover_limits_and_customer_excess` deductible column | no | **yes** | no | kept; required |
| 350.00 | `service_benefits_each_plan_carries` food-spoilage row | no | **yes** | no | kept; required |
| 12.00, 15.00, 35.00, 30.00 | `premium_arrears_and_ending_fees` late-fee, admin-fee and transfer-fee columns | no | yes for the 12.00 the late-fee baseline reads | no | kept; required |
| 8.00 | `the_fee_carried_by_each_unpaid_period` tier value | **yes** (task 0's tier) | no — the periods and the rate are absent | no — 24.00 and 30.00 are absent | kept; the render contract requires a tier value in figures |
| 6.50 | `writing_part_of_a_late_fee_off` tier value | **yes** | no | no | kept; required |
| 15.00 | `the_household_excess_on_spoiled_food` tier value | **yes** | no | no | kept; required |
| 15.00 | `the_charge_for_raising_a_premium_invoice` tier value | **yes** (task 1's tier) | no — the 124.02 total is absent | no — 136.54 is absent | kept; required |
| 35.00 | `the_loading_for_claims_already_filed` tier value | **yes** | no | no | kept; required |
| 22.50 | `the_reduction_for_a_prompt_report` tier value | **yes** | no | no | kept; required |
| 60.00, 30.00 | `the_allowance_a_managed_care_agreement_carries` tier values | **yes** for 60.00 | no | no | kept; required |
| 18.00 | `the_handling_charge_on_an_invoiced_settlement` tier value | **yes** | no — the 202.50 excess owed is absent | no | kept; required |
| 12.00 | `the_part_of_an_excess_deferred_for_late_billing` tier value | **yes** | no | no | kept; required |
| 30.00 | `working_out_a_food_spoilage_allowance` household-excess default | baseline, so by construction non-governing | yes | no — 82.00 is absent | kept; a baseline must state its own constants |

**The conjunction is never satisfied.** Where a governing tier's value is printed, it is printed as a rule,
and the base it would apply to is not in that document; where a base is printed, it is printed in a schedule
that applies no tier to it. The nine facet schedules, every ladder threshold in figures, and every policy
constant a ladder or baseline must state are therefore correctly kept — and keeping them is not optional:
revision 1's own bijection test would have recorded a threshold named under a business term but never stated
in figures as a red light.

### 7. R2-01 — confirmed

The corpus nowhere says the `overwrite` was narrowed, and nowhere asserts that the base's billing-day
provision fixes the extended instalment period. Checked three ways. The overwrite registry is unchanged from
revision 1 — seven entries across five base clauses on `protection_premium_delinquency` (two),
`protection_agg_payout_cap` (two), `protection_excl_duplicate_coverage`, `protection_premium_billing` and
`protection_claim_settlement`. `how_premium_is_billed_and_applied` cl. 2 is unchanged in substance and still
reports the clause as *"**no longer in force**, having been superseded by the current basis on which an
instalment is priced. What that basis produces is not restated here"*, with the unnamed remainder still in
force. And a corpus-wide search for `narrow*`, `confined to (the) fleet|business`, and `only (on|for) (the)
business fleet` returns nothing. The instalment period now comes from the charter's own new sentence,
carried verbatim in `billing_a_premium_instalment_period`: *"The instalment is billed for the period running
from the plan's billing day in the month reached to the day before that day in the month following."*

Revision 1's reading of the rationale's claim is unchanged and still correct: the rule is confined, but by
an **invoicing** condition, not to the fleet tier, and no document repeats the tier claim. The renderer was
right to decline it.

### 9. New findings introduced by the round-2 change

Two, both policy-side, both reported because the remit is to report every problem.

**R2-N1 — the narrowing left a dangling retirement.** The `overwrite` on `protection_premium_billing`
retires the clause "an instalment plan bills the monthly premium of the plan on the same day of each month"
**unconditionally**, and that clause is the base's whole statement of what an instalment plan bills and when.
The round-2 carve-out then sends the plans the narrowed rule no longer reaches back to it:

> `rule` / `billing_a_premium_instalment_period`: "A plan whose premium is not invoiced to such an account is
> priced as the premium billing rules of the product state, and nothing in this rule changes what it pays."

Those rules no longer state it. Task 0's plan is exactly such a plan — `premium_plan: monthly_instalment`
with no store credit account on the profile — so for it the corpus now names a provision that the same
`overwrite` has removed. Consequence: no scored value on either task turns on it (task 0 needs no instalment
billed, every reached period being already billed, and its arrears policy prices its own period ahead by its
own rule), and a reader is not stranded in practice, since `premium_tariff_schedule` still states 12.99 as
the plan's monthly premium and the ledger shows the pattern. But the retirement is now wider than anything
in force replaces, and the carve-out is a dangling reference. The KB renders both the retirement and the
carve-out verbatim from the source, so the faithful side is the document and the defect is in the charter's
structure. Not a KB verdict.

**R2-N2 — "the one standing scheduled" is singular where the records need not be.** The new source sentence
reads *"The care agreement read is **the one** standing scheduled on the profile"*, and the binding is
`CFIELD('service','service_agreement_id', status='scheduled')`, which resolves one record. Where a profile
held two care agreements standing scheduled, neither the rule nor the corpus says which is read. Immaterial
on both tasks' worlds — task 1 holds exactly one, standing scheduled; task 0 holds two, both `completed`, so
none is read and no allowance arises. The KB reproduces the source's wording exactly, so the softness is the
source's and the KB correctly does not close what the source leaves open. Not a KB verdict.

### bijection_verdict (revision 2)

**PASS.** Revision 1's single finding B1 is closed at its root — the charter was amended in favour of the
prose, the binding now agrees with the ladder, the threshold of one is gone from the corpus, and the KB
carries the amended ladder, its new status sentence and its new term-versus-remainder sentence verbatim. The
whole domain corresponds losslessly: 15 base policies, 3 measures, 8 extended policies with 8 baselines and
39 factor ladders complete tier by tier, 5 retired clauses written as retired with their unnamed siblings in
force, 8 tool contracts, and 6 prerequisites carried verbatim on the blocked side in the declared `state`
form, each in exactly one document of the corpus. Nothing was added: the three definitional sentences
revision 1 traced to bindings are now sentences of the source's own rules, and the two new definitions (the
attendance-charge class, the allowance-as-money reading) are verbatim from the charter. No new
document-side defect. The two new findings are policy-side and are reported without changing this verdict.

### dependency_form (revision 2)

**PASS.** No regression on any of the fourteen checks of revision 1, each re-run: no state-form sentence
restated as an action; no tool, policy id or document named outside its own hub; no dependency or order
stated that no prerequisite sentence states; no sentence carried in a second document; no dependency table,
checklist, roadmap, route or cross-problem step list; no cross-problem operational guidance; no
wrong-versus-correct contrast and no example walking across problems; no task-mirroring title or opening; no
depended-on document reachable only through the dependent document's phrasing; no factor document naming a
tier a customer falls on, describing the mistake to avoid, or writing a task's evidence rows in as a fact; no
computation document hinting at variation; no factor naming a computation document or a sibling. Two
additions were examined specifically and neither goes beyond the source's form: the instalment rule's
carve-out names "the premium billing rules of the product", which is a general subject and not a document, a
